Status

FinKore Core 2.0.5 stable.

Purpose

This document defines the minimum meaning and content of an Audit Event. An Audit Event records a domain occurrence; it is not required to be the Business Event itself or the source from which domain state is reconstructed.

Requirements

  • AUDIT-EVENT-001 — Every committed Audit Event MUST have a stable event identifier, event type, entity reference, and timestamp.
  • AUDIT-EVENT-002 — It MUST identify an Actor when the responsible Actor is known; otherwise Actor attribution MAY be omitted or explicitly represented as unknown.
  • AUDIT-EVENT-003 — The event type MUST be a stable, producer-supplied domain event identifier. In Core 2.0 it MUST be a non-empty ASCII token matching [A-Z][A-Z0-9]*(?:_[A-Z0-9]+)*. FinKore does not define a closed global event-type catalog in Core 2.0. Implementations MUST NOT derive event type automatically from TypeScript method names, class names, repository methods, HTTP endpoints, database operations, framework callbacks, or other implementation mechanism names.

    Research / Clarifies a boundary

    Preserving collected traces does not prove capture of required events ↗

    Surendra Kumar Valavala

    Domain event identity, complete event fields and preservation of committed records do not demonstrate capture of every required occurrence. The conceptual framework motivates an independent coverage question.

    Scope and limitations

    A separate expected workload can test coverage if it is independent of the collector. This is not a mandate to record every request or collect sensitive content indiscriminately. A diagnostic retry trace is not itself a unique financial effect.

  • AUDIT-EVENT-004 — The entity reference MUST identify the affected entity type and stable entity identifier.
  • AUDIT-EVENT-005 — The timestamp MUST identify an unambiguous instant when the recorded occurrence took effect and, when serialized, MUST follow Timestamp conventions.
  • AUDIT-EVENT-006 — Event metadata MAY provide relevant context.
  • AUDIT-EVENT-008 — Event metadata MUST NOT contradict required event fields.
  • AUDIT-EVENT-007 — In Core 2.0, an Audit Event is complete when every required Audit Event field is present and individually valid according to this document and referenced actor, timestamp, entity, change, and redaction requirements. No additional event-type-specific fields are required by Core 2.0. Optional metadata or display text MUST NOT be required to recover the event identifier, event type, entity reference, timestamp, known actor identity, or recorded changes.

  • AUDIT-EVENT-009 — Event metadata MAY be omitted or supplied as any JSON value, including explicit null, subject to AUDIT-EVENT-008. An implementation MUST preserve its presence and recursively preserve its JSON value, including every object member name. Omitted metadata and supplied null metadata MUST remain distinguishable. Cyclic containers and unsupported native values MUST be rejected with FINKORE_AUDIT_INVALID_EVENT during non-actor Event representation validation under AUDIT-ERROR-004. Shared acyclic containers are not cycles. Accepted values MUST be retained and observed independently of caller mutation under AUDIT-APPEND-001; rejection MUST leave logical history unchanged under AUDIT-ERROR-001.

For an Event supplied specifically as redaction evidence, the otherwise-open metadata value is refined by AUDIT-REDACTION-010. That operation-specific linkage requirement does not reserve redactionEvidence on ordinary Events or change the general metadata profile.

Audit Relationships, when present, follow Audit Relationships.

Metadata value profile

AUDIT-EVENT-009 uses the existing JSON-value boundary for Actor metadata and ordinary Change values, without introducing a numeric representation or coercion policy. Supported native numeric classes remain language-specific and must preserve exact, independent values. An implementation must not repair an unsupported value by dropping it, coercing it to a string or number, or replacing a cycle with null. Names such as __proto__ and constructor are ordinary JSON members. Metadata does not change the existing required-field contradiction rule or validation priority.

Invariants

Within one audit history, event identifiers must be unique and committed events must follow append-only behavior.

Example

The following JSON is illustrative and non-normative; it does not prescribe serialized member names.

{
  "eventId": "evt-1042",
  "eventType": "ENTITY_SUBMITTED",
  "entity": { "type": "expense", "id": "exp-52" },
  "actor": { "type": "user", "id": "user-7" },
  "occurredAt": "2026-08-31T10:15:30Z",
  "changes": []
}

Invalid Examples

  • An event with only free-form prose and no event type or entity reference.
  • Reusing an event identifier within the same history.
  • Supplying a calendar-invalid occurrence timestamp, an unknown -00:00 offset, or more than nine fractional digits.

Open Questions

  • Must ingestion time be recorded separately from occurrence time?
